summary.description: Hexachlorobenzene is a white crystalline solid, volatile and insoluble in water but dissolves in organic solvents, fats, and oils. It was historically used as a fungicide and in manufacturing chlorinated solvents.
emission_sources: Past use as a fungicide on cereal seeds
Natural releases from fires and volcanoes
environmental_impact: Persistent in the environment and bio-accumulates in the food chain
Can damage liver, immune, and reproductive systems at high exposures
Induces birth defects and accumulates in fish, marine mammals, and some plants

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: HCB exposure at high levels causes liver damage, immune and reproductive system harm, and birth defects, posing significant risks to human health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: HCB bio-accumulates in aquatic organisms including fish and marine mammals, threatening marine biodiversity and ecosystem health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Due to its persistence and toxicity, managing HCB as a by-product of industrial processes and past pesticide use is critical for sustainable consumption and production practices.
